A.explanation: Product $\sigma A = 50 \times 10^6 \times 1.5 \times 10^{-5} = 750 \text{ N}$, which is less than $4000 \text{ N}$ so 4.0 kN would already exceed the elastic limit.

B.explanation: Product $\sigma A = 80 \times 10^6 \times 1.5 \times 10^{-5} = 1200 \text{ N}$, which is less than $4000 \text{ N}$ so 4.0 kN would cause plastic deformation.

C.explanation: Product $\sigma A = 50 \times 10^6 \times 7.5 \times 10^{-5} = 3750 \text{ N}$, which is still less than $4000 \text{ N}$ so 4.0 kN would just exceed the elastic limit.

D.explanation: Product $\sigma A = 80 \times 10^6 \times 7.5 \times 10^{-5} = 6000 \text{ N}$, which is greater than $4000 \text{ N}$ so 4.0 kN remains within the elastic region.

hints: Notice the 4.0 kN compressive force does not cause plastic deformation, so the stress due to 4.0 kN must be at or below the elastic limit stress $\sigma$.
Recall compressive stress is $\sigma = F/A$ with $F$ in $\text{N}$, $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $\sigma$ in $\text{Pa}$, where $1 \text{ MPa} = 10^6 \text{ Pa}$.
Rearrange to the survival condition $\sigma A \ge 4000 \text{ N}$ and test each $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ with each $\sigma$ in $\text{Pa}$ to see which pair can support at least 4.0 kN.
walkthrough: Identify the limit: the cylinder stays elastic under $F = 4.0 \text{ kN} = 4000 \text{ N}$, so the applied stress at 4.0 kN must not exceed the elastic limit $\sigma$.
State the rule for stress: $\text{stress} = F/A$. The elastic condition is $F/A \le \sigma$.
Rearrange to a test on the pair: $\sigma A \ge F$, i.e. $\sigma A \ge 4000 \text{ N}$ for a possible elastic-limit pair.

Convert $\sigma$ from $\text{MPa}$ to $\text{Pa}$ by multiplying by $10^6$, then calculate $\sigma A$. For example $7.5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^2 \times 80 \text{ MPa} = 7.5 \times 10^{-5} \times 80 \times 10^6 = 6000 \text{ N}$.

Compare with $4000 \text{ N}$: the $1.5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^2$ pairs give only $750 \text{ N}$ and $1200 \text{ N}$, and $7.5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^2$ with $50 \text{ MPa}$ gives $3750 \text{ N}$, all below $4000 \text{ N}$.
Only $7.5 \times 10^{-5} \text{ m}^2$ with $80 \text{ MPa}$ gives $6000 \text{ N} > 4000 \text{ N}$, so 4.0 kN produces a stress below the limit. This is option D.
